newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean imports up 47 pct Jan-March - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean imports up 47 pct Jan-March - Safras.

text.p: Brazil already imported 160,200 tonnes of soybeans in the first three months of this year, 47 percent above the 109,200 tonnes imported in the corresponding period in 1996, consultant Safras e Mercado said.
Soymeal imports totaled 55,400 tonnes in January to March 1997 against zero imports in the first three months of 1996, it added in its weekly report.
Only in the case of soyoil has the pace been slower, with imports reaching 32,300 tonnes against 60,100 tonnes in January to March 1996.
Of the 160,200 tonnes soybeans bought this year, 57,700 tonnes have come from the U.S. and the bulk from Paraguay.
Paraguay also sold Brazil 51,600 tonnes of its soymeal imports, with the remaining 3,800 tonnes coming from Argentina.
Total soybean imports are likely to reach 1.8 million tonnes this year, 92 percent above the 937,000 tonnes brought in in 1996, Safras said.
Principal suppliers are likely to continue to be Paraguay and the U.S., Safras said.

In the case of soymeal, Brazilian purchases are expected to amount to 200,000 tonnes against 79,000 tonnes last year, while soyoil imports in 1997 Safras estimated at 250,000 tonnes, 50 percent above last year.
The high imports in the case of soybeans and soymeal are due to anticipated record soybean exports, currently forecast to reach eight million tonnes.
